records.deidentified_narrative: unit 1 collided with ped at the 6400 block of fm 78. when i arrived ped was laying on the ground and having a hard time breathing. ped had visible injury to his face and chest. ems made the scene and ped was transported to sammc with life threatening injuries. i talked to the driver of unit 1 and he stated ped walked into the path of his vehicle while he was traveling westbound at the 6400 block of fm 78. the driver of unit 1 stated he tried to avoid ped but he collided with ped with the right side of his vehicle. the driver of unit 1 did not show any signs of intoxicants and had a good license and insurance. the driver of unit 1 did not complain of any injuries and his vehicle was not towed due to damage. i then notified tid and sgt. both sgt and tid made the scene. csi was also on scene and processed the scene. there was also a witness who saw the accident and her information is listed. officer hillman #0847 talked to her and she observed [roadway] into the path of unit1. i then gave the driver of unit 1 a [case id] and released him after tid completed their investigation. officer c. harris #1196 checked the status of ped and it was determined that he was in critical condition with several broken bones in his chest. i was not able to identify ped as it is assumed that ped might be homeless. i find ped at fault for walking into the path of a moving vehicle. no further action at this time. coban and bwc is available.

[roadway] spur 354 and was struck by unit 1. unit 1 was traveling s/b [roadway]. unit 2/pedestrian failed to yield right of way to motor vehicle, causing unit 1 to collide front concentrated to the left side of unit 2/pedestrian. unit 2/pedestrian traveled s/b approximately [roadway] of s/b traffic. unit 1 left the location without stopping to render aid. dfd rescue 43 responded to the scene and found unit 2/pedestrian to have no vital signs at 4:14 am on [date]. medical examiner j. scott responded to the location and took possession of unit 2/pedestrian body. medical examiner [case id]. vcu detective 8357, traffic sgt 7230 and crime scene element [identifier] responded to the scene. unit 2/pedestrian is homeless and did not have any identification on his person, so he had to be identified by his fingerprints. witness d. johnson said that he was walking s/b on the east sidewalk of [roadway] and saw unit 2/pedestrian walking e/b across the s/b lanes of traffic. he said that he saw the gray/silver car and a white car traveling s/b [roadway]. he said that he heard the impact, then he saw something flying in the air and thought that it was a barricade sign. he said that he did not know that it was body, until he got to it. he said that after the impact both cars stopped near the body, then left the location. he said that he thinks that the gray/silver car hit unit 2/pedestrian. witness dpd officer j. saucedo said that he was in a nearby parking lot and heard the big thump and thought it was an accident, so he turned and saw a guy flying in the air. he said that [roadway] and blocked the scene, then he got out to check on unit 2/pedestrian and that unit 2/pedestrian did not appear to be alive. a couple of minutes after this crash, unit 1 was involved in single vehicle crash in the [roadway]. the responding officers arrived on scene and observed the broken, bloody windshield of unit 1 and determined that it was the related to this fatality crash. i/o responded to the scene of unit 1 second crash to investigate the crash. see related [case id] for state crash report. i/o inspected the damages to unit 1 front end and windshield and determined that they were consistent with those caused by unit 2/pedestrian body hitting the hood and front windshield. i/o also determined that unit 1 color is the same as the color of the paint chips left at the scene of the fatality crash. unit 1 had extensive damage from the second crash and all the air bags were deployed, so it is unknown if the airbags deployed during the fatality crash or during the second crash. unit 1 driver was under the influence of drugs. this report is incomplete pending toxicology results for unit 1 driver and for unit 2/pedestrian. ***** this report was supplemented by i/o #8502 on [date] to include blood results for unit 1 driver and unit 2/pedestrian. the blood results for unit 1 driver showed to be positive for alcohol and positive for drugs. ethanol: 0. 063 +/- 0. 011g/100ml. drugs: carboxytetrahydrocannabinol: 15. 8 +/- 3. 2ng/ml. the blood results for unit 2/pedestrian showed to be negative for alcohol and drugs. i/o also added the information for unit 1 driver that was changed/removed by txdot. this report is now complete. *****

records.deidentified_narrative: attached full narrative to sheet as an attachment on sunday, september 16, 2018, at 1548 hours, i, officer e. benavidez, 4609, working as [identifier], was dispatched to a major accident at [roadway], the sam’s club, with officer c. hoffman 4618, officer alarcon 4440 and sgt hennard 3718. a few call details are as follows;“sams club - silver honda car vs sams club building - medstar ntfd”“... racks fell on people in the store”upon arrival, at 1550 hours, i noticed a white dodge charger by the walmart parking lot, unit 2,it looked as if it was just involved in an accident but the car did not match the call descriptions so i proceeded to the call location. however, officer hoffman stayed with unit 2 and the driver of unit 2, allen, cynthia michelle (bf [date]) relayed to him that as she was driving south in the parking lot, unit 1 was cutting west through the parking spaces. unit 1 stopped right in front of her, in her direction of travel, not giving her enough time to maneuver around him to which the two units collided. shortly after their vehicles made contact, both cars came to a complete stop and the driver of unit 1 and 2 made eye contact with each other and unit 1 drove south away from [roadway] and proceeded to take a u-turn into the sams club parking lot and went north towards the store and unit 1 through the south wall of the store. a report number was given to cynthia on scene for the accident that included the entire incident. there were 3 witnesses to this initial minor accident; mcmatton, bryan (wm [date]), sugden,charles bm [date], and lobby, christy (bf [date]). all the witnesses stated that the driver of unit 1 was driving through the parking lot of walmart and right in front of unit 2 and after they collided, he proceeded to the sam’s club parking lot and drove into the wall of the store. as officer hoffman was speaking with cynthia, i approached the sam’s club at [roadway]., i saw a hole in the south wall and beyond the hole was unit 1 sitting in the bakery isle with significant amount of damage done to that particular side of the store. i proceeded around the car to see the driver of unit 1, shah,subhash (am [date]) with medstar personnel and gathered information about what had just occurred. i spoke with subhash and he advised me that a car hit him in the parking lot and that his brakes gave out and he had no control over the vehicle and that [roadway] through the wall of the sam’s club. however, as i tried to gather more information from him, he had trouble with articulating the scenario due subhash not speaking very much english but he was able to tell me the majority of what occurred during our conversation. i looked to my left and saw bailey, tamera (bf [date]), amidst the debris, lying on the floor and unable to get up. she stated to me that she was hit by falling shelves as unit 1 drove through the building. i asked witnesses, dimick,tom ([date] )and baxter,jessica (wf [date]), who were caring for tamera’s possible injuries about what they saw and tom stated that he and jessica were standing by the bakery isle when unit 1 drove through the south side wall of sam’s. the vehicle proceeded to knock down not only merchandise but shelves across the area and tamera was standing by one of those shelves when they hit her, however, she was not hit by unit 1. medstar personnel tended to tamera and she advised them that her neck and her back were hurt and was eventually taken to jps by medstar 55. tiu was notified and sgt mapes advised that an accident report should be done. subhash ‘s son, shah,subhashchandra (am [date]) arrived on scene shortly thereafter and i made him aware of the incident. he asked his father what transpired, subhash told him that someone’s vehicle hit his vehicle from behind and knocked his vehicle through the wall of the store. subhash had also told other witnesses this same story, and when subhashchandra asked me where the other vehicle who hit his father was, i proceeded to show subhashchandra the rear of unit 1 and he agreed that there was not significant damage that would indicate that scenario being possible. subhash was eventually taken by medstar 30 to medical city of arlington. i then relocated to walmart, where subhash’s original location was before the incident to see if their security footage had captured the incident. i was informed that the only evidence that was captured of the incident was unit 1 driving through the sam’s club south wall. cass,michael (bm [date]), a walmart representative, was able to save the video and advised me that he would have it ready if further information was required from the video evidence. officer hoffman then spoke with the on-duty manager at sams, aelgre,jonathan (wm [date]) who also stated to him that the video of the incident was captured on their cameras and would submit it to detectives if a further investigation was necessary. unit 1 was taken by denny’s towing and the manager on duty was given a report number of the incident and advised officers that he had no further information. pictures and videos of the incident were taken and uploaded to evidence. com no cssusgt. hennardsgt. hennard 3718-axon not activatedunit#218-0170-no dash-h220e. benavidez 4609-axon activated-unit#218-0010-no dash-h215c. hoffman 4618-axon
